messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: negative binomial confusing doc
parts:
I don't have posting privileges to stan-devel, so I'll post here (I emailed too, overkill is good :) ).

What makes negative binomial parametrization complicated includes the scale vs. rate parametrization choice for the gamma, and the question is the negative binomial the distribution of k failures before r successes (r is fixed, k starts at 0), or how many trials are needed before r failures (r is fixed, k starts at r), or a Poisson/Gamma mixture. It's all, of course, but that changes the meaning of some of the parameters.

In the first (Gelman) version, Gelman uses the rate parametrization of the Gamma, but calls it "inverse scale" instead of rate (which is correct, rate = 1/scale), so calling it "inverse scale" in the NBinom is consistent (as is done in Appendix A of BDA3).

The second version is an alternative parametrization of the Negative binomial based on its variance to mean (which is 1 + inverse scale) but the V2M is not one of the explicit parameters. Doing it this way makes the NB depend explicitly on the mean as one of its parameters. Running through the algebra, mu, being the mean, is equivalent to Version 1's alpha / beta and so phi must be equal to alpha. To be consistent, I would call phi there the shape as per version 1, and call mu either the mean or location. Phi isn't the inverse scale any more than alpha is--they are identical.

R itself refers to alpha/r/phi as the "size" as well as "shape" (due to its being the gamma's shape).

Of course, to my continued frustration, the parametrization I use for the negative binomial is the one where beta is the scale itself, not the rate or V2M (as per DeGroot or Klugman, Panjer, Wilmot), so I'm used to seeing :

NB = Choose(r + k -1, k) * (b / (1+b)) ^ k * (1 / (1+b)) ^ r

Where r = alpha = phi and my_beta = 1 / your_beta = mu / phi.

Which makes for a loglikihood of:

lnΓ(r + k) - lnΓ(r) - lnΓ(k + 1) + k * ln(b) - (r + k) * ln(1 + b)

which I think is simpler than the other two. I'd request that be added too, but I understand if you feel having three negative binomial parametrizations in Stan and its documentation is a harbinger for the zombie apocalypse.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] negative binomial confusing doc
parts:
Thanks --- that was really helpful.

I think we'll eventually add more negative binomials.
The parameterizations really make a difference for MCMC,
both for HMC samplers like Stan and for Gibbs samplers like
JAGS.

I think having multiple parameterizations is good in that it
simplifies the models and helps prevent coding errors. I just
want consistent doc so the errors don't get introduced in
interpreting the functions.

I think what would be nice is a big table of how to
inter-translate parameters in all the different parameterizations.

I'd also like

I think we may eventually move to some even more Stan-friendly
parameterizations, like a normal parameterized with log standard deviation,
for example. It would make it easy to use a lognormal prior and also
saves a transform plus Jacobian and trades a log for an exp in the
density computation.

And some parameterizations that are better suited to hierarchial priors,
like a beta and dirichlet on the mean/total count scale.

Anyone have any suggestions on naming conventions? I'm unhappy
with neg_binomial2, but it seemed better than just passing
on suffixes indefinitely, like neg_binomial_shape_inverse_scale.
We've used the scale elsewhere, as in poisson_log() and multi_normal_cholesky().

- Bob
